reading.title: The Ball That Tells Time
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述课文里的 Town Hall 大钟，而是讲一个真实的公共计时仪式——纽约时报广场的新年落球，以及它与航海“报时球”的历史渊源。内容改编自时报广场官方机构(Times Square Alliance)的权威资料。

source.title: History of New Year's Eve & the Times Square Ball

passage: Long before glowing screens counted down the seconds, communities relied on a single shared signal to keep their clocks honest. The most ingenious of these was the time-ball, a large sphere mounted on a pole that dropped at a fixed instant each day. The first such device was installed atop England's Royal Observatory at Greenwich in 1833, and its purpose was strictly practical: ship captains anchored in the harbour would watch for the descent and, at that precise moment, calibrate their chronometers, the delicate instruments on which safe navigation depended. Roughly 150 of these public time-balls eventually appeared worldwide, though almost none survive today.

From this maritime tradition sprang one of the planet's most famous public rituals. When fireworks were banned in New York as a hazard, organisers needed a new spectacle, and in 1907 the very first New Year's Eve ball, an iron-and-wood sphere weighing some 700 pounds and studded with a hundred light bulbs, descended above Times Square. The crowd was no longer there to set its watches; the falling ball had been transformed from a humble navigational aid into a symbol of collective celebration. Over the following century its design was reinvented repeatedly, recast in lightweight aluminium and later sheathed in faceted crystal.

What endures is not the object but the impulse behind it. Each year hundreds of thousands of people converge on one square, and roughly a billion more watch from afar, all synchronising their attention to one descending light. The time-ball thus illustrates a curious reversal: an instrument once prized for cold precision has become a vessel for shared emotion, proof that a community will always gather around whatever it agrees to call the moment.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the main idea of the passage?
options: Atomic clocks have made the Times Square ball drop scientifically obsolete.
A device invented to keep clocks accurate gradually became a shared celebration.
Fireworks remain the safest way to mark the arrival of a new year.
Ship captains in Greenwich invented the modern New Year's Eve party.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文主线是：报时球本是为了校准时钟的实用工具，后来演变成全民共享的庆祝仪式，所以选 B。

questions.question: According to the passage, where and when was the first time-ball installed?
options: In Times Square, New York, in 1907.
On a harbour pier in the United States in 1955.
At the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, England, in 1833.
Aboard a navigation ship in the early nineteenth century.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中明确说 The first such device was installed atop England's Royal Observatory at Greenwich in 1833，所以选 C。

questions.question: Why did ship captains watch the time-ball drop?
options: To set their chronometers at a precise moment for safe navigation.
To celebrate the start of the new year with the crowd.
To signal that fireworks were about to begin.
To count down the final seconds before midnight.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中说船长在落球的精确瞬间 calibrate their chronometers，而航行安全依赖这些仪器，所以选 A。

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about why the ball drop survived after fireworks were banned?
options: People wanted a cheaper alternative to atomic clocks.
The government required every city to keep a time-ball.
Ship captains in New York still needed to set their chronometers.
Organisers needed a new public spectacle and the falling ball provided one.
questions.explanation_zh: 文中提到烟花被禁后 organisers needed a new spectacle，落球正好填补了这个需求，由此可推断选 D。

questions.question: In the final paragraph, the word "synchronising" most nearly means
options: coordinating at the same time.
competing against one another.
gradually losing interest.
traveling a long distance.
questions.explanation_zh: synchronising their attention to one descending light 指大家在同一时刻把注意力对齐到同一个落球上，即“同步、协调一致”，所以选 A。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 9 的五个倒计时句式提升到 B2+：用更正式的语境设置特殊日期、写人群在事件前已聚集、从过去视角描述即将发生之事、用 waited and waited 表现漫长等待，再用 began to laugh and... 写群体情绪的转变。语法锚点不变，但句子更长、更抽象。

patterns.title: It was the last day of ...
patterns.source: It was the last day of the year.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 It was the last day of... 设置一个特殊日期，让读者立刻知道这一天为什么重要。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句(更抽象的语境)：写某个时代、计划、考察任务或一段共同经历的最后一天，并暗示它的意义。
must_include: It was the last day of
patterns.sample: It was the last day of the long expedition, and a strange mixture of relief and sadness settled over the exhausted crew.
patterns.tip_zh: of 后面接一个时间阶段或活动，比如 the year、the term、our trip。

patterns.title: a large crowd of people had gathered ...
patterns.source: A large crowd of people had gathered under the Town Hall clock.
patterns.focus_zh: had gathered 表示在主要事件发生前，人群已经到齐并等在那里。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句(更复杂的语境)：写在某个重要时刻到来之前，一大群人已经聚集在某地，并加上他们的状态或期待。
patterns.sample: Long before the ceremony was due to begin, a large crowd of people had gathered in the freezing square, breath rising in the lamplight.
patterns.tip_zh: had gathered 后面最好接地点，这样画面会更清楚。

patterns.title: would ... in ...
patterns.source: It would strike twelve in twenty minutes' time.
patterns.focus_zh: would 表示从过去那个时刻看，某件事很快将要发生；in 后面接还要等多久。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句(更抽象的语境)：从过去某一刻的视角，写一个具有象征意义的事件再过多久就会发生。
patterns.sample: According to the official schedule, the historic launch would begin in less than thirty minutes, and the tension in the control room was almost unbearable.
patterns.tip_zh: 这里的 in 不是地点，而是“再过多久”。

patterns.title: We waited and waited, but ...
patterns.source: We waited and waited, but nothing happened.
patterns.focus_zh: 重复 waited and waited 能写出等待太久的感觉，再用 but 接期待落空。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句(更复杂的语境)：写你们带着强烈期待长久等待某个信号或结果，但它始终没有出现，并写出由此产生的情绪。
patterns.sample: We waited and waited for some confirmation to appear on the silent screen, but the figures never changed, and a quiet unease spread through the hall.
patterns.tip_zh: but 后面写没有发生的结果，句子才有转折。

patterns.title: began to laugh and ...
patterns.source: Everybody began to laugh and sing.
patterns.focus_zh: began to laugh and... 写人群从紧张或尴尬转向轻松、庆祝的反应。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句(更抽象的语境)：写在尴尬或紧张之后，一群人的情绪突然转变，开始大笑并做出某种集体反应。
patterns.sample: After an awkward silence that seemed to last forever, the whole audience began to laugh and applaud, as if the failure itself had become the best part of the night.
patterns.tip_zh: and 后面接第二个动作，可以把情绪变化写完整。
